name: Christmas holidays
title: Christmas holidays
intro: Christmas markets and snow, Santa in Lapland or a beach in the sunshine. Here's where to go on holiday over Christmas, near and far.
seo_title: Christmas holidays: where to go for markets, snow or sun

sections.heading: Christmas markets for a short break
sections.text:
Most of Europe's big Christmas markets open in the second half of November and run until just before Christmas, and a few stay open until early January. Two or three nights is enough for most of them. Going on a weekday, or before December, means smaller crowds and cheaper hotels.

- **[Colmar](/destinations/colmar):** six small markets in a fairytale old town of painted houses and canals. The prettiest of them all, and the most crowded at weekends.
- **[Strasbourg](/destinations/strasbourg):** one of the oldest Christmas markets in France, spread across the old town, half an hour by train from Colmar. Our guide to [Strasbourg or Colmar at Christmas](/blog/strasbourg-or-colmar-at-christmas) helps you choose, or do both.
- **[Riga](/destinations/riga):** a cosy market on Dome Square in a cobbled old town that claims the world's first decorated Christmas tree, and much cheaper than western Europe. Cold, often below freezing.
- **[Tallinn](/destinations/tallinn):** a market in the medieval Town Hall Square, often under snow.
- **[Cologne](/destinations/cologne), [Nuremberg](/destinations/nuremberg) and [Dresden](/destinations/dresden):** the classic German markets, with mulled wine, gingerbread and wooden toys.
- **[Vienna](/destinations/vienna) and [Prague](/destinations/prague):** grand city squares lit up, with plenty to do indoors when it's cold.
- **[Copenhagen](/destinations/copenhagen):** Tivoli Gardens becomes a Christmas village of lights and rides; see our guide to [Tivoli at Christmas](/blog/tivoli-gardens-at-christmas).

For more, see our [best Christmas markets in Europe](/blog/best-christmas-markets-in-europe), or skip the airport with [Christmas markets by train from London](/blog/christmas-markets-by-train-from-london).

faqs.question: Where are the best Christmas markets in Europe?
faqs.answer: Strasbourg, Colmar, Nuremberg, Dresden and Cologne have some of the oldest and biggest. Vienna, Salzburg, Prague, Budapest and Bruges are lovely too. Most run from late November until just before Christmas, though some stay open until New Year.

faqs.question: Where can we meet Santa at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Finnish Lapland is the classic choice. Rovaniemi has Santa Claus Village on the Arctic Circle, while Levi and Saariselkä are smaller and quieter, with Santa visits, huskies and reindeer in the forest.

faqs.question: Where can we have a white Christmas?
faqs.answer: Lapland and Tromsø are almost certain to have snow. In the Alps, high resorts like Zermatt are the safest bet, and Innsbruck and Salzburg often have snow in the mountains nearby.

faqs.question: Where is warm at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, Fuerteventura and Tenerife are about four hours away and usually around 20 to 24°C. Further afield, the Caribbean, Thailand, Goa, Sri Lanka and the Maldives are in their dry season, and Cape Town and Sydney are in summer.

faqs.question: When should we book a Christmas holiday?
faqs.answer: As early as you can. Christmas and New Year are the busiest and dearest weeks of the year to travel. Going in early December, to see the markets before the school holidays, is often much cheaper.
